requirements.evidence: Contract is complete: Queues.php:24-283 exposes every required property/method (name, creating, viewingQueueId, confirmingToggle, editingQueueId, renameName, accessQueueId, managingAccess; openCreate/closeCreate/create/openQueue/closeQueue/startRename/cancelRename/rename/confirmToggle/cancelToggle/toggleActive/openAccess/closeAccess/grantAccess/revokeAccess) and passes accessQueue/accessGrants (Queues.php:269-277); Serve.php:24-171 implements selectedQueueId, mode, locked lastCalledTicketId, notice and callNext with the required exception notices; routes/web.php:59-60, layout navbar, lang keys and members tabs (members.blade.php:7-32) are all present. Gaps are small: mode is not constrained to the three allowed values (Serve.php:33,83), several text buttons lack aria-labels (queues.blade.php:52,134,187), and child modals open on top of the still-active detail modal (queues.blade.php:61,93,120,143).

conventions.evidence: Good parts: domain writes go through CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess (Queues.php:84,159,229,225/241), authorization uses policies, views use Bulma and x-label/x-input (queues.blade.php:44-46). Deviations: public input properties lack #[Validate] and create()/rename() never call $this->validate() (Queues.php:27,48,79-96,144-167; Serve.php:33), helpers callableQueues()/selectedQueue() are public although internal (Serve.php:109,125), and no docs/CHANGELOG/PHPDoc updates ship with the new public API.

security.evidence: Strong: every client id is resolved scoped to the entity with findOrFail (Queues.php:98,127,152,189,202-224; Serve.php:72), entity and lastCalledTicketId are #[Locked] (Serve.php:24,39), all output uses escaped {{ }} (queues.blade.php:16-24, serve.blade.php:53-72), and successful calls are rate-limited per user+entity (Serve.php:75-98). Gaps with limited impact: openQueue() exposes a queue without $this->authorize() (Queues.php:96-104, guarded only by the mount gate), and name/renameName/mode reach the domain unvalidated at the component boundary (Queues.php:27,48; Serve.php:33).

tests.evidence: The only test changes are in tests/Feature/Entity/MembersTest.php:377,398,416 and tests/Feature/Entity/EntityInviteTest.php:185. There are no tests for app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php or app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php, so neither new component has happy-path, validation, unauthorized-call or tamper coverage.

simplicity.evidence: The code is direct: one small addDomainErrors helper (Queues.php:283-291), action calls instead of new services, and no speculative abstractions. Minor redundancy: render() passes callableQueues and tickets as aliases of queues and waitingTickets (Serve.php:148-152) although serve.blade.php uses only $queues and $waitingTickets.

readability.evidence: Names and structure mirror app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php, and docblocks explain the untrusted client state (Queues.php:30-54; Serve.php:27-42). Readability is only slightly reduced by the public helper methods (Serve.php:109,125), duplicate view-data aliases (Serve.php:148-152), and the multi-modal state spread across four view blocks (queues.blade.php:61-143).

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task: two new components (Queues.php, Serve.php), their two views, two routes (routes/web.php:59-60), lang keys in both locales, navbar links (default-page.blade.php:44,50), the members tabs (Members.php:38,47; members.blade.php:7-32) and the test updates those tabs required. No unrelated refactors or features.

issues.explanation: Neither new Livewire component ships with a single test, while the project requires test-first development and the Livewire definition of done (happy path, validation failure, unauthorized call and tamper attempt for every action), so the change cannot merge as is.

Public user-input properties name, renameName and mode have no #[Validate] rules and create()/rename() never call $this->validate(), violating Livewire rule 1 and leaving all input validation to the domain actions.
openQueue() resolves and exposes a queue without calling $this->authorize() on it, so it is protected only by the mount-level create check instead of authorizing the action itself as rule 3 requires.

mode is never validated against any/priority_only/normal_only; callNext() and waitingTickets() silently coerce a tampered value to CallMode::Any, so the effective mode can disagree with the selected option and no error is raised.
The detail modal remains is-active whenever viewingQueue is set, so opening rename, toggle or access renders two aria-modal="true" dialogs simultaneously instead of suppressing the parent dialog.
The task asks every interactive control to have an aria-label, but the create/rename submit buttons, the confirmation toggle button and the access footer close button rely on visible text only.
callableQueues() and selectedQueue() are public Livewire methods even though only the component uses them, contrary to the rule that only methods genuinely callable from the front end stay public.

issues.location: CHANGELOG.md and docs/ (not present in the diff)
issues.explanation: No CHANGELOG entry, documentation update or PHPDoc on the new public methods accompanies the change, although the conventions require docs to stay in sync.
The locale test now asserts only the two tab labels, so the previously covered invite form strings are no longer asserted anywhere after the invite UI moved behind the invites tab.
render() passes callableQueues and tickets as duplicates of queues and waitingTickets, but serve.blade.php never uses the aliases.

review.summary: The change adds the Queues management page and Serve panel as new Livewire components with views, routes, both-locale lang keys, navbar links, and a tabbed members page. The required flows and tenant-scoped resolution are largely correct, but neither new component has any tests, and the components skip the mandatory Livewire input validation and per-action authorization patterns, so the pull request needs changes before merging.
